solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Start with determination but can't finish?

definitions.text: Start with determination but can't finish?

parts.words: Start with determination but can't finish?
parts.note: to tackle a task with gusto is the idiom meant; read another way, someone who is stuck and cannot go on fails to finish

explanation.surface: Someone launches into a job with gusto but never manages to complete it.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works both ways: as an idiom it means pitch in eagerly, while taken literally it describes being stuck somewhere and unable to get out or finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to pitch in enthusiastically is to begin a task with real vigour.

clue.text: Receives and doesn't remember forgoing

indicators.note: split as 'for going', it says the letters f-o-r go away from the start

parts.note: someone who doesn't remember forgets

explanation.surface: A forgetful person accepts things and loses track of what they gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgoing' looks like 'doing without', but read as 'for going' it tells you to drop FOR from FORGETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to obtain or be handed something is to acquire it.

clue.text: He made-up stories about wonders

indicators.note: invented, so the letters of the two words are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: A storyteller spins invented tales about marvels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made-up' looks like an adjective for the stories but signals rearranging HE and STORIES; 'wonders' is a verb here, not the marvels of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to speculate or form hypotheses is to ponder possibilities.

clue.text: Cure to be enjoyed

definitions.meaning: to cure an illness is to deal with it medically
a special pleasure, such as a delicacy or outing

explanation.surface: A remedy that is pleasant to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a doctor attends to a patient's illness, and a delight is something special laid on for pleasure.

clue.text: Home from prison, embracing the new tot

indicators.note: the prison word holds the other piece in its arms, so it goes round it

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement

indicators.note: made new, so the word tot is given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A family brings their new toddler home after a spell in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' is not 'out of prison' but the definition, a small rural house.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small country house is a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Set to work and I constructed a cover as replacement

indicators.note: the rebuilt 'and I' letters are made into a cover that goes round the other piece
built anew, so the letters of 'and I' are assembled in a fresh order
the word set is put to work, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gets busy and builds a stand-in covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' turns SET into STE; 'constructed' turns AND I into INAD, which serves as 'a cover' around STE. 'cover' looks like the definition, a stand-in, but the definition is 'as replacement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done in place of another is done as a substitute or stand-in.

clue.text: The man beside him provided the seat

definitions.text: The man beside him provided the seat

parts.words: The man beside him provided the seat
parts.note: the clue treats him as a boy's name; that name with the word man placed beside it gives a low padded Turkish-style seat

explanation.surface: A man sitting next to someone gave up his chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' stands for the answer: a man's name which, with MAN after it, gives a low upholstered seat or footstool.
explanation.definitionFit: Name puzzle: a German boy's name that, joined with man, forms a footstool or couch.

clue.text: The Heartless Male is what the lecture's on

indicators.note: without its heart, the word male keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A talk is about a cruel man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' looks like a description of the man but tells you to keep only M and E of MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the subject of a talk is its topic.

clue.text: He's not trained to get a crack at acting

indicators.note: drilled and shaped, so the letters of these words are reshaped
cracked open, these letters break apart and re-form

explanation.surface: An untrained man still wants a shot at being an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' and 'crack' both signal the anagram of HE'S NOT plus GET A; 'a crack at' is not the idiom it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: working in the theatre as a performer is being in the profession of drama.

clue.text: I told you so! You must get right inside

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right goes within the old word for you

parts.note: thee is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A smug speaker insists their listener has to go in correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is archaic THEE, with R placed 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamation: a triumphant interjection said when proved correct.

clue.text: Will have accommodation to house teams playing

indicators.note: the shelter word takes in the other letters as residents

parts.note: a tent is basic camping accommodation

indicators.note: teams at play move about, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: There will be lodging for visiting sports teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as a verb but is the noun, a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a last will is a legal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: Sits jogging on. Animal is cooperative

indicators.note: one piece placed on, that is after, the other

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: jogged about, the letters of sits are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for a docile beast: it sits, then jogs on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means the scrambled letters are placed after the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who helps or lends a hand is being helpful to others.

clue.text: Tear off to back the car in. It's a busy life

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other
gone off, the word tear is scrambled
backing the car means reading its letters in reverse

explanation.surface: A driver rushes off to reverse into a parking spot, in a hectic existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles the first word to RATE, and the reversed car goes inside it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the competitive, frantic struggle of modern working life.

clue.text: The skin wasn't firm, you say

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: something that wasn't firm swayed to and fro

explanation.surface: Someone complains a leather hide felt slack.
explanation.walkthrough: SWAYED and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soft napped leather is a kind of animal hide.

clue.text: Hoping sound of quartet will find wanting

parts.note: hoping is wishing

indicators.note: the spoken form of the number for a quartet is what counts

parts.note: a quartet is four

explanation.surface: Optimistic about the noise a string quartet will make, but finding it lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like 'lacking' but is the definition, meaning desiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: desiring something is longing to have it.

clue.text: Is not going all out again to get ahead

indicators.note: the letters of is not go all out of their places and rearrange

parts.note: RE is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to give maximum effort a second time in order to succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going all out' signals reshuffling IS NOT, followed by RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: coming in the future, as with surprises that await us.

clue.text: 'Have done wrong before' is a previous clue

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
done wrong, its letters are set in an incorrect order

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A confession that someone erred earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: a crossword clue already met in the list going downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: the first clue in the vertical list, referring back within the puzzle.

clue.text: Cool? Not even close

definitions.meaning: far away, a long way off

explanation.surface: Is someone unfriendly? They're not even nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: emotionally remote and standoffish, and physically far away.

clue.text: Seen quickly, a label with name on

indicators.note: the name is put on, that is after, the label

parts.note: a tag is a label
Lance is a man's name

explanation.surface: A name tag spotted in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: perceived immediately, with only a brief look.

clue.text: Is in possession of the figures and loses no time

parts.note: to be in possession of is to have
tens are figures, numbers of ten

explanation.surface: An accountant holds the numbers and acts quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: HAS plus TENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who hurries is making haste.

clue.text: Crack egg in battered flounder

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a crack player is a star

indicators.note: beaten about, the letters of egg are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: break an egg into batter to coat a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounder' looks like the fish but is the verb, to stumble; 'battered' rearranges EGG to GGE, which goes 'in' STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to struggle clumsily is to totter or lurch.

clue.text: 'The horse fly,' you add, 'returned'

indicators.note: turned back, the joined words are read in reverse

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
to add is to sum

explanation.surface: A conversation about a horse and a fly, with someone chipping in that it came back.
explanation.walkthrough: GNAT followed by SUM, the whole read backwards because of 'returned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: After a jiffy, free policeman

indicators.note: the freeing word comes after the moment word

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a jiffy
to untie is to free

explanation.surface: An officer is released after a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, British slang for a moment, then UNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

clue.text: Made up?

parts.note: something fabricated is untrue, which is what a flat denial says

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is invented.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat retort, meaning 'that's untrue', answers the charge that something is fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a denial that a claim is true, so the claim is fiction.

clue.text: Time and again in the enclosure

indicators.note: one piece is set in the other
the outer word acts as a pen holding the inner one

parts.note: RE is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Repeatedly found in the paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time and again' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Time' is the definition, an hour of the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an hour on the clock, as in meeting at that o'clock.

clue.text: English town where Under-ground is taken by almost all

indicators.note: the scrambled word is taken into the other piece
nearly all of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: the word as written before trimming

indicators.note: ground up, the letters of under are reworked

explanation.surface: A town where most people ride the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL; 'ground' rearranges UNDER to RUNDE, which 'is taken by' AL. ARUNDEL is a castle town in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a West Sussex market town known for its castle.

clue.text: Closed when decorated

definitions.meaning: fastened, as with buttons or a zip
refurbished, as a house is renovated

explanation.surface: A shop that shut while being refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of a phrasal verb: fastened clothing, and renovated or redecorated a property.

clue.text: Leave shut up? That is surprising!

parts.note: to leave is to go
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Telling someone to depart and be quiet, then marvelling at it.
explanation.walkthrough: GO plus SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamation: a mild interjection expressing astonishment.

clue.text: Badly torn in struggle that lasts some time

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other

parts.note: a fight is a struggle

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of torn are out of order

explanation.surface: A long, grinding contest leaves someone's clothes ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters go in just after the first letter of the struggle word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a period of fourteen days, two weeks.

clue.text: Dog half cut, bounding round

indicators.note: half of the word bounding is cut away, keeping its back half

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A tipsy hound leaping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' looks like British slang for drunk but signals keeping the second half of BOUNDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a wild Australian canine.

clue.text: Is sorry to say it's a ploy

indicators.note: signals the word spoken, which sounds like the entry

parts.note: a ruse is a ploy

explanation.surface: Someone regrets admitting their scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: RUSE and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to regret is to feel remorse.

clue.text: Why one didn't get charged with being politically incorrect?

definitions.text: Why one didn't get charged with being politically incorrect?

parts.words: Why one didn't get charged with being politically incorrect?
parts.note: charged means accused, but also billed: the talk cost nothing, and the right to say offensive things is protected

explanation.surface: A puzzle about why someone escaped prosecution for offensive remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' reads as prosecuted, but also means billed: the remarks came at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the right to express opinions without censorship.
